Take rates are unchanged, so revenue falls with volume and the deterministic (median-input) FDV -61.2% to $1.24B; implied price $0.90. Current 30d volume $4.48B is 87% of the 30d record $5.15B; the trigger fires at -40%.

scenarios.title: Solver cartelization: HHI_solver > 3,500, 1Click loses the spread

Minimum wall-clock span of the solver sample before the cartelization trigger may grade HHI_solver breached or clear. The method-filtered execute_intents pages and settlement-hub legs typically cover a window of minutes; fills inside a 2-minute window are serially correlated (the same solvers quote consecutive blocks), and the bootstrap CI resamples only within that window, so it measures within-window noise, not how concentration varies across hours. One hour is the shortest span that spans several quoting cycles; the range runs from 15 minutes to one day.

Number of method-filtered NearBlocks execute_intents pages (50 receipts each) in the stratified solver sample: the newest page plus pages placed at even time offsets back to solver_sample_target_span_s. Each page is one block of the page-block bootstrap, so more pages tighten the HHI_solver CI. Unauthenticated NearBlocks served 5 solver calls after the caller walk and refused the 6th (HTTP 429, 2026-11-08), so the walk runs in chunks of 5 one rate window apart: 6 to 10 pages cost the same single extra ~62 s window, and 8 = 5 + 3 leaves headroom in the second window. ~400 receipts spread over hours versus the 4 contiguous pages (~3 minutes) used before.

Target time depth of the deepest solver-sample page (6 h), reached by jumping NearBlocks' id cursor rather than walking page=N (page >= 2 without a cursor answered HTTP 520 after 50 s on 2026-11-08). Deeper cursors cost latency: 1.4 s at ~5 h, 2.0 s at ~11 h, 14 s at ~41 h, 40 s at ~7 days (measured 2026-11-08). 6 h is 6x the solver_sample_min_span_s floor, so a misaimed cursor still clears it, and spans the Asia/Europe/US session hand-offs inside one run; the range runs from the 1 h minimum to 12 h (latency still ~2 s).

Scorecard threshold: a flow share (confidential volume, AI-agent-labeled receipts) is called 'material' at >= 10% of the measured total; below it the claim is graded NOT_SUPPORTED. A conventional materiality line, not a fitted value.

fee_pool_share.headline: NEAR Intents takes 27.3% of the six-protocol cross-chain fee pool over the 30 days to 2026-11-21, rank 2 of 6 behind Relay at 40.8%; its rolling 30-day share moved from 35.0% to 27.3% over 182 days (low 2.5% on 2026-09-13, high 45.3% on 2026-07-04) and the linear trend (-5.37 pp per 30 days, 90% interval -8.61 to -2.14) is falling, with the interval excluding zero.
fee_pool_share.read: Cuts against the bull case: NEAR Intents is losing share of the fees these routers collect, so fee growth has to come from the pool growing, not from share capture. It is overturned by a positive share trend whose 90% interval excludes zero. Relay collects 1.5x NEAR Intents' fees under its own adapter's definition. NEAR Intents' own 30-day fees went from $2.90M to $7.42M over the window; the pool went from $8.30M to $27.23M. With Relay excluded the share is 46.0% against 48.8% at the start of the window (-1.35 pp per 30 days, 90% interval -2.31 to -0.39).
caveats: Fee share is not volume share: a router charging more per dollar routed has a larger fee share at the same volume. DefiLlama's bridge-volume API is paid, so no volume-side comparison is made here.

Adapter fee definitions differ, so the pool sums unlike quantities; each adapter's own text is quoted next to its protocol (`protocols[].methodology_fees`). The ex-Relay share is published because Relay's adapter counts integrator app fees and swap costs.
The common window is 212 days (2026-04-24 to 2026-11-21), set by Relay's first day; the trend describes these months only.
Routers outside DefiLlama's fee coverage (LI.FI and other aggregators) are absent, so the pool is these six protocols, not the cross-chain market.
Rolling 30-day points overlap by 29 days; the interval uses a Newey-West error with 60 lags, and the daily non-overlapping share trend is reported as a cross-check.
THORChain is measured by DefiLlama's `thorchain-dex` adapter (swap, outbound and affiliate fees); the `thorchain` slug is the chain's native transaction fee and is not a routing fee.

The share path is not a line: it ranged from 2.5% (2026-09-13) to 45.3% (2026-07-04) and the linear trend explains 47% of its variance. Read the slope as the average drift over the window, not as a forecast.

Relay's 30-day fees peaked at $205.95M on 2026-09-22, 14.7x its window median of $14.04M. NEAR Intents' share around that date moves with that surge in the denominator, not with a change in its own fees. Whether the surge is user-paid routing fees or an adapter artefact cannot be settled from this endpoint.

THORChain DEX reports zero fees on 38 days of the window (longest run 37 days, 2026-05-16 to 2026-06-21). The zeros are kept as reported; if they are an adapter gap, the other protocols' shares are overstated for rolling windows that include those days. See the robustness share excluding it.

wide_peers.reading: The cap is at or below the upper quartile of the set (1,512x), so the model's terminal value does not rest on a multiple richer than what the market pays for chain revenue today. On L1 gas revenue alone NEAR (4,327x) is priced above the wide median (363x), so NEAR is not cheap on chain revenue; the long-term case has to be carried by Intents revenue, not by the L1 multiple. This reading is overturned if a re-run puts the cap above the 75th percentile of the set (peer multiples compressing toward 60x) or if the set shrinks below 8 peers.

backtest.method: Rolling-origin out-of-sample test of the SOTP volume GBM. At each origin the model is calibrated only on days up to the origin (V_0 = trailing 30-day volume / 30; sigma = volume_volatility over the trailing 365 days via sotp _sigmas; drift = the run's public_volume_growth_yoy with the Ito correction) and the lognormal law of 30-day volume at month h is compared with the realized 30-day sum ending round(h x 30.44) days later. Closed-form quantiles of the model's own GBM; no simulation.
not_tested: fee take rate (public and confidential) and its compression toward the floor
confidential share of volume and its drift to the target share
terminal FDV/revenue multiple and discount rate
caveats: Forecasts at h = 3 and 6 months from monthly origins overlap, so their errors are serially correlated: the effective sample is smaller than n and the binomial interval is too narrow for those horizons.
public_volume_growth_yoy is a registry assumption chosen with the full history in view; the 'measured drift' variant removes that look-ahead by using only the trailing mean monthly log return.
The series is total NEAR Intents volume; the live model splits it into public and confidential legs with the same sigma, so the split itself is not tested.

block_bootstrap.label: Stationary block bootstrap of daily log-changes, resampled drift
block_bootstrap.method: Stationary block bootstrap (Politis-Romano: geometric block lengths, circular wrap) of realized daily log-changes of volume over the trailing 365 days up to the origin. Mean block length: Politis-White (2004) automatic selector with the Patton-Politis-White (2009) correction on that lookback, capped at min(3 sqrt(n), n/3); rule fixed from the series' autocorrelation before any coverage was computed. 10,000 paths (the valuation Monte Carlo's count), seed 20261114 mixed with the origin timestamp. Each path continues the daily series from the origin day; the forecast is the sum of the last 30 days of the path at the horizon, scored against the same realized 30-day sums as the GBM.

calibrated.rule: exact two-sided binomial test of P10-P90 coverage vs 80%, p >= 0.10

registry_drift.label: Block bootstrap, demeaned and rescaled to the GBM's expected path (shape only; the form fed to the Monte Carlo)

rule_of_thumb_blocks.label: Sensitivity: mean block length n^(1/3) instead of the Politis-White selector (resampled drift)

caveats: Nothing in the bootstrap is tuned to reach 80% coverage. With about 20 origins, choosing block length, lookback or path count by coverage would be overfitting; the block rule and path count were fixed first and the n^(1/3) block rule is shown only as a sensitivity.
Low power: the exact binomial test on about 20 one-month origins accepts a wide range of true coverage, and 3- and 6-month forecasts overlap, so a pass is weak evidence of calibration, not proof.
A bootstrap can only replay changes that occurred in the lookback. It widens the band where the past year was volatile and cannot anticipate a regime the lookback did not contain.

Daily volume carries day-to-day noise that reverses. Blocks shorter than that reversal overstate horizon variance, so part of any coverage gain can come from a wider band, not a better-shaped one; the band-width ratio is reported for that reason.

The path starts at the origin day's volume, one noisy observation, and the registry-drift form holds the mean path fixed, so a wider distribution mechanically lowers its median. Both are stated properties of the design, not fitted choices.

No second design was tried after these results. Resampling changes of the 30-day sum instead of daily volume would remove the day-to-day noise, but choosing between engine designs on about 20 origins is the tuning this test rules out; it is left as a stated next test.
The valuation still runs on the GBM. The bootstrap is a parallel variant; no headline figure uses it.

comparison.headline: The block bootstrap does not repair the volume engine: P10-P90 coverage (1m 19/20 (95%, p 0.16), 3m 17/17 (100%, p 0.03), 6m 12/14 (86%, p 1.00)) is rejected against 80% for over-coverage at 3m; the pass at 1m and 6m rests on about 20 origins, which is weak evidence; its band is 2.1x to 3.2x the GBM's log width, so it covers by being wide, not by being sharp; the GBM is rejected at 2 of 3 horizons (1m 14/20 (70%, p 0.26), 3m 10/17 (59%, p 0.06), 6m 7/14 (50%, p 0.01)), so the two engines bracket realized dispersion and neither is calibrated.

volume_12m.unit: multiple of the current trailing 30-day volume

fdv.method: Base Monte Carlo rebuilt from the snapshot (same inputs, seed, path count). Bootstrap run: same price, take-rate and issuance paths and the same expected volume path; monthly volume = V_0 (1+g)^t x monthly mean of exp(demeaned block-resampled daily log path), normalised to mean 1 per month. Only the dispersion of volume changes.

valuation_effect.headline: The valuation uses the GBM. At the same expected path the bootstrap puts 30-day volume 12 months out at 0.13x / 0.73x / 4.28x of current (P10 / P50 / P90) against the GBM's 0.59x / 1.61x / 4.39x, a band 1.7x as wide in log terms; through the same Monte Carlo FDV P10 / P50 / P90 becomes 0.13x / 0.28x / 0.77x of the base. The backtest rejects the bootstrap for over-coverage, so read this as a stress bound on volume dispersion (with the mean path held fixed, a wider distribution lowers the median), not as a better central estimate.

take_rate_series.method: Inner join of the DefiLlama near-intents daily charts (gross fees, revenue, holders revenue, dexs volume). Rolling 30-day take = sum(fees) / sum(volume) x 1e4 bps over 30 consecutive settled days (net uses revenue, holder uses holders revenue). Trend = OLS of ln(rolling gross take) on time in years, change per year = exp(slope) - 1, 90% CI from a Newey-West standard error with a 60-day Bartlett lag (twice the window, because consecutive rolling points share 29 of 30 days). Elasticity = OLS of ln(daily gross take) on ln(daily volume), Newey-West 30-day lag, days with zero fees or volume dropped. Trailing days dated on or after the run date, and up to 3 trailing days with revenue above fees, are excluded.

take_rate_series.headline: Gross take compressed over the trailing year: the rolling 30-day rate is 18.7 bps on 2026-11-26 against 21.0 bps a year earlier, while average daily volume went from $124M to $143M; the trailing-365d log-linear trend is -26% per year (90% CI -41% to -8%), which excludes zero, and the trailing-180d trend, +76% per year (90% CI +55% to +101%), does not show the decline continuing.
take_rate_series.investor_read: This cuts against the bull case: gross take fell at 26% per year over the trailing year with an interval that excludes zero (non-overlapping check: -21% per year, 90% CI -36% to -3%, also excludes zero), so the claim that pricing power has held while volume grew is not supported by the fee history; the level is still 37x the 0.5 bps model floor. The trailing-180d trend is +76% per year (90% CI +55% to +101%): the decline is not visible in the last six months. A trailing-365d interval that includes zero again would overturn this read; a 180d interval wholly below zero would show compression still in progress. NEAR's captured (net) take went from 2.1 bps to 3.9 bps over the same span and sat under the 3 bps fee-race trigger on 266 of 365 trailing rolling points.
caveats: Early history mixes fee regimes: the DefiLlama fee chart ramps from zero in mid-2025 and net revenue is zero until the first sweep, so the full-history trend measures fees being switched on. Read the trailing-365d figures.

Fees, revenue and holders revenue follow DefiLlama's near-intents adapter definitions: gross fees include the affiliate fee each frontend keeps; revenue is NEAR swept into the revenue wallets and is booked on the sweep day, so net take is lumpy and can exceed fees on single days. An adapter revision restates the whole series.

Rolling 30-day points overlap (29 of 30 days shared), so about 12 independent observations sit in a year. A Newey-West interval on such points is too narrow at this sample size: in the seeded null simulation in quant/tests/test_take_rate_series.py a trendless series is flagged well above the nominal 10% of the time. The non-overlapping 30-day check (Student-t) stays near its nominal size and is the stricter read: treat a trend as established only when both intervals exclude zero. An interval that includes zero means no decline was detected, not that none exists.
The elasticity regresses fees/volume on volume: noise in daily volume enters both sides and pushes the estimate negative.
